label: Late-episode D1 after a reward, staying with a2
explanation: Fires only at D1, only when the reward input is 1 (previous trial rewarded), only late in the episode (no activity before trial ~55; rate rises steeply from trial 70 and is highest at trials 80-99), and almost only when the previous choice was a2 and the agent is about to choose a2 again (the upcoming choice is the agent own computation; its policy logit at those steps sits in a moderately a2-favoring band [-4.4,-1.5]). Its activation also coincides with low value-head output (<7.1). It never fires at GO or D2, after unrewarded trials, or when the previous or upcoming choice is a1. From the example windows, magnitude seems to grow with episode trial index and over runs of rewarded a2 trials (e.g. 0.11, 0.15, 0.18, 0.22, 0.26 on consecutive rewarded D1s); I only checked this by reading examples. The low-activation misses are mostly trials just below the trial-78 cutoff. The trial-index threshold suggests the feature partly encodes elapsed episode time. No future variables are used: action at D1 is the agent own upcoming choice.

skeptic.revised_label: Late-episode D1 after a common a2 -> S2 reward, staying with a2
issues: Systematic false-positive class: the label and predicate cover any rewarded D1 after a previous a2 choice, but the feature essentially never fires when that reward came through a RARE transition (a2 -> S1, rewarded). On dev, (D1)&(in_rew==1)&(action==2)&(prev_action==2)&(prev_common==0) has 12070 predicted steps and precision 0.0012. Rare-rewarded a2 trials make up most of the original predicate's false positives, and the test misses output shows them repeatedly (a cell marked *r1* with no activation following an 'a2 S1R' trial).

Replacing prev_action!=1 with prev_common!=0 raises dev precision from 0.808 to 0.905 (F1 0.856 -> 0.907) and test F1 from 0.843 to 0.903 (precision 0.780 -> 0.889) at the same recall. Using prev_state!=1 instead gives the same result (dev F1 0.909). So the feature encodes a reward from S2 reached commonly via a2 (the case where the model-based policy says stay with a2), not just 'reward after a2'.

The magnitude figures in the explanation (0.11, 0.15, ...) are fractions of the maximum activation, not raw values. The mean activation is 1.02 and the max is 2.58. The strongest activations (about 1.0 of max) come at rewarded D1s that follow unrewarded trials, so magnitude does not simply grow with runs of rewards. This claim is only partly supported.

Claims that check out: active only at D1 (0 activations at GO and D2); only when in_rew==1; about 0 activations with upcoming action a1 (1 step) or previous action a1 (43 steps); none before trial 50 and a steep rise from trials 70-89; value < 7.13 in 99.9% of the activation mass; policy logit in [-4.44, -1.52] for 98.6% of the mass. The test scores the other agent reported are reproduced (F1 0.843). The predicate uses no future variable that the agent couldn't compute: action at D1 is its own upcoming choice, and prev_common is observed.

final_label: Late-episode D1 after a common a2 -> S2 reward, staying with a2
